headline: Majors hold above 200s on strong multi-week uptrend, but today's selloff and extreme long crowding into weakening momentum warn that the rally is straining.
paragraphs: All seven majors sit above their 200-day moving averages. None have yet reclaimed the 50-day line, and no golden cross has formed: the regime is uptrend-in-progress without confirmation from the slower frame. Bitcoin down 3.6% on the day but up 19.6% on the week and 21.2% on the month; Ethereum down 3.4% daily but up 26.6% weekly and 30.2% monthly. The smaller caps have run harder: Solana up 34.7% on the week, XRP up 37.9%. This is a market that has built real distance in seven to thirty days while today's tape shows fatigue. The dominance structure supports the majors: Bitcoin holds 59% of total market cap even as altcoins rally, suggesting capital flowing within a hierarchy rather than rotation into true speculation.

Momentum is rolling over against trend. Across the board, RSI-14 readings sit between 53 and 74, with Bitcoin at 68.9, Ethereum at 68.6, and Solana at 73.7. These are not overbought extremes (those live above 80), but they are elevated, and the MACD is above signal on every asset, yet every single symbol lost ground on the day. This is the technical signature of a rally that has exhausted its intraday push: momentum remains positive in the medium term but lacks fresh buyers at current prices. Solana's RSI at 73.7 is the tensest read; combined with Solana down 4.99% on the day after a 34.7% week, the asset is showing classic high-velocity exhaustion. Smaller names like Dogecoin and Cardano, which sit below their 200-day lines (Doge and ADA both false) and carry RSI readings of 59.2 and 53.3 respectively, are already broken from the uptrend structure, though even they are positive on the month.

Positioning is crowded and expensive. Bitcoin perp funding annualizes at 11%, Ethereum and Dogecoin also at 11%, with 8-hour rates of 0.01% across majors. These are not panic lows; they are the level you pay to hold leverage long in a rising market. Open interest is substantial: Bitcoin at $2.26 billion, Ethereum at $1.50 billion. The long-short ratio tells the fuller story: Bitcoin 1.18, Ethereum 1.41, Solana 1.55, Dogecoin 3.83, XRP 2.36. Every major is skewed long, with smaller caps showing extreme imbalance. Over the last 7 to 24 hours, liquidations have favored shorts: Bitcoin saw $20.7 million in long liquidations against $1.8 million in shorts; Ethereum $17.2 million in longs versus $4.1 million in shorts. This is the exit pattern for longs taking profits or being shaken out after a big move, not the pattern of a market ready to accelerate further. The ratio of long-to-short liquidations is roughly 10:1 in Bitcoin and 4:1 in Ethereum. When you have this much leverage long and this imbalance in how losses are distributed, a reversal day can cascade.

Flows paint a mixed but telling picture. Bitcoin ETF net inflows reached $1.43 billion over the last five sessions and $242 million on 27 Aug alone, with nine consecutive days in the same (inflow) direction. This is vanilla institutional bid: spot, not leveraged, and persistent. Ethereum has added $898 million over five sessions with the same nine-day streak. Yet whale exchange flows show $184 million of Bitcoin moving off exchanges over the last 24 hours, net. The weekly data shows this reversal in progress: Aug 7 saw $316 million off exchanges; Aug 14 and Aug 21 saw $405 million and $831 million move onto exchanges, respectively; this week (ending Aug 28) $620 million onto. Stablecoin float sits at $309.3 billion, essentially flat month-on-month (up 0.88%). The contradiction is real: traditional finance (ETF flows) is steady and long, but big holders are trimming exchange inventory and did so heavily in the last two weeks. When ETF buyers and whale sellers act in opposite directions after a 35% alt rally and a 19% Bitcoin rally, the question is whether the ETF bid can absorb the supply being taken off the table.

Sentiment is at 73, labeled Greed, in a 30-day range of 25 to 74. The top end of the range arrived today on a down day for every major, which is the classic setup for a squeeze: fear and greed are both extremes. The stablecoin float is not elevated; dry powder is sparse. When the crowd is greedy and cash is already deployed, the tape usually needs a new catalyst to rally from here, not just existing bid. Bitcoin and Ethereum 12-month highs are 38% and 48.5% away; even the weaker performers like Cardano and Dogecoin are 70%+ below their highs. There is a lot of history between current price and prior peaks, which is mathematical room to run, but also a lot of broken trend above current levels that would need reclaim. Bitcoin network difficulty is falling by 1.2% into the next retarget (1,184 blocks out), a sign of declining hash power, though this can be noise in the shorter window.

Watch for two conditions: a move in Bitcoin above $80,268 (the 7-day high) without fresh liquidations of shorts, which would signal buyers stepping in on a breakout bid rather than longs getting shaken; and a reversal in ETF flows from inflow to outflow, which would close the gap between institutional and whale positioning. If the long-short liquidation imbalance persists into the next session with price holding above the 200-day but RSI rolling over, the setup turns fragile. A reclaim of the 50-day line by Bitcoin would confirm the trend; failure to hold above 200 would signal the uptrend breaking. Stablecoin float under 0.5% movement is a floor, not a ceiling: if it rises sharply in the next few days, the message is that dry powder is being raised in anticipation of lower prices.
